description: Pairwise alignment with the TWO-PIECE (dual) affine gap model of ksw2 / minimap2 (ksw2_extd2): a gap of length k scores max(gapOpen1 + k*gapExtend1, gapOpen2 + k*gapExtend2) (a short-gap and a long-gap regime; all four gap numbers are scores <= 0, ksw2's q + k*e cost is gapOpen = -q, gapExtend = -e; defaults = minimap2 -A 2 -B 4 -O 4,24 -E 2,1), Gotoh's O(m n) program with two gap states per direction, mode 'global' (end to end) or 'local' (Smith-Waterman), optional diagonal band (ksw2 w: only the cells |i - j| <= band; a global alignment needs |m - n| <= band). VERIFICATION: 1 600 committed cases (400 global, 400 local, 400 banded global, 400 banded local; scores equal Biopython 1.88 PairwiseAligner with the callable gap score and an independent Waterman-Smith-Beyer program, every alignment re-scores to its score). Z-drop / end-bonus extension alignment is the separate tool ksw2_extend.

mismatch.description: Score of a different pair (minimap2 -B is the penalty: -4).

gapOpen1.description: Short regime: gap open score (<= 0; minimap2 -O first value as -4).

gapExtend1.description: Short regime: gap extension score per position (<= 0; -E first value as -2).

gapOpen2.description: Long regime: gap open score (<= 0; -O second value as -24).

gapExtend2.description: Long regime: gap extension score per position (<= 0; -E second value as -1).

band.description: Band half-width (cells with |i - j| <= band); -1 = full matrix.

format.description: Optional output format; the alignment written in that format is returned in the result field 'formatted'. Biopython Bio.Align names: fasta, a2m, clustal, phylip, nexus, stockholm (byte for byte as Bio.Align.write; 'emboss:' + name selects the EMBOSS writer of the same name). EMBOSS -aformat names: pair, simple, srspair, srs, markx0, markx1, markx2, markx3, markx10, match, score, sam, tcoffee (two rows) and msf, mega, meganon, nexusnon, paup, paupnon, phylipnon, selex, treecon (any number of rows; EMBOSS prints the run date: now, UTC). Omit for no formatted text. This pairwise tool (it knows its sequences) also writes the alignment in the COORDINATE formats of Biopython 1.88 Alignment.format, byte for byte: bed (bed3 ... bed12), psl, chain, maf, sam (sam:md adds the MD tag), exonerate (exonerate:cigar), and the strings cigar (cigar:eqx = extended = / X; soft clips for the unaligned query), md (SAM MD tag) and cs (cs:long; minimap2 difference string). In those formats sequence1 is the target (reference) and sequence2 the query, except for the semi-global tools where sequence2 is the reference (target); the plain name sam is the Biopython SAM line (the EMBOSS one is 'emboss:sam'); a 'bio:' prefix forces the coordinate writer.

names.description: Optional names of the rows for the formatted output (default seq1, seq2, ...).

trimEndGaps.description: Coordinate formats (bed, psl, chain, maf, sam, exonerate, cigar, md, cs): drop the leading and trailing columns that have a gap in one row (the free end gaps of a semi-global result), so that the record starts and ends with an aligned pair (Biopython alignment[:, first:last]); false (default) keeps them as D / I blocks as Biopython's PairwiseAligner does (2D4M2D).

endPosition1.description: 0-based inclusive end (length − 1 for a global result).

endPosition2.description: 0-based inclusive end (length − 1 for a global result).

formatted.description: The alignment written in the requested format (null when format is omitted).

errors.message: mode is not global / local; a gap score is positive; band < -1; a global band narrower than |m - n|
